disease_label_per_paper: Massive pericardial effusion in acute pericarditis with slight short-duration ST-segment elevation; viral pericarditis assumed
presentation_summary: 77-year-old woman presented with sudden continuous chest pain and shortness of breath.
Initial examination showed temperature 38.4 C, blood pressure 111/74 mmHg, pulse 90/min, and no clear pericardial friction rub.
Initial labs showed WBC 10,200/uL, CRP 5.5 mg/dL, CK 47 IU/L, LDH 115 IU/L, creatinine 0.6 mg/dL, NT-proBNP 2710 pg/mL, and negative troponin T.
ECG had no abnormality up to 5 hours after admission, then slight ST-segment elevation was observed in most leads at 15 hours.
Echo and CT initially showed small circumferential pericardial effusion; by day 6 circumferential effusion increased to 20-25 mm with pleural effusion and worsening bilateral heart failure.
